speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness. To help me understand the severity and origin of these symptoms, how long have you been experiencing them?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That fluctuation with activity and specific positioning of your double vision is very characteristic. To confirm this, do you experience drooping of your eyelids or a slurred speech when you are tired?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of ptosis/diplopia worsening with fatigue, ocular symptoms triggered by gaze direction, and symmetric proximal limb weakness without sensory deficits or fever is classic for this autoimmune neuromuscular junction disorder.
